answer.generated: Data augmentation in deep learning serves to artificially expand the training dataset by applying transformations to existing images, thereby increasing the diversity of the training data and improving model robustness. This technique differs from regularization methods such as weight decay or dropout, which primarily aim to prevent overfitting by adding a penalty term to the loss function or introducing randomness during training, respectively. While data augmentation directly increases the quantity and variety of training samples, regularization techniques modify the optimization process to control model complexity, thus indirectly enhancing generalization.
